openings.claim: Move tracking of required and transferred pieces into a reusable staging map drawn with existing pencils on existing tally sheets: one labelled position per required piece for the current pattern. Vacant positions expose incomplete picking; pieces remaining after filling expose incomplete transfer. This evaluates an unproven full-workshop intervention through a bounded probe.
openings.delta: Unlike material tags or a remote sample, the map carries each kit's physical completion state beside its envelope. Volunteers fill every position, transfer its contents, and close only after the map is empty. They remain responsible for correct material, dimensions, one piece per position, and pattern assignment; pencil the pattern onto the envelope. Maintenance includes drawing maps, changing them between patterns, replenishment, and clearing each cycle; all count toward the two volunteers' 90 minutes.
openings.prediction: With the same pattern mixture and local supply access, mapped staging will expose missing picks or incomplete transfers before closure more often than loose staging, without changing specified contents. A 60-kit run could meet the target only if setup and checking also fit 90 minutes.
openings.rival_prediction: The nearest alternative is loose materials beside each volunteer, as in O4. If proximity and reduced interference explain improvement, loose staging will match mapped staging's completeness and finish sooner because it avoids map maintenance.
openings.defeat: A paired probe finds equally few corrections with loose staging, while maps add time; or envelopes still omit pieces despite apparently completed map cycles. Failure to fit the layout on the existing table defeats this implementation under C3.
openings.probe: Using exactly two volunteers and existing supplies, first measure two single-kit maps plus supplies against the table footprint. Within the 90-minute ceiling, compare small matched-pattern batches with loose and mapped staging, alternating order. Include setup, replenishment and contents audit; record visible vacancies, leftovers, corrections and total time. Stop if the footprint fails. A small batch cannot establish 60-kit success.
assumptions: Existing tally sheets have sufficient usable space for maps.
Two single-kit maps and necessary supplies fit the table.
Pattern quantities and dimensions can be represented legibly.
Map handling and checking leave sufficient time for all 60 kits.
